verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the church of God that is in Corinth, with all the saints who are in all of Achaia:
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassions and God of all comfort,
verses.1:4: who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those in any affliction through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
verses.1:5: For just as the sufferings of Christ abound toward us, so through Christ our comfort also abounds.
verses.1:6: Now if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; or if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which operates in the endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer,
verses.1:7: and our hope for you is firm, knowing that just as you are sharers in the sufferings, so also you are in the comfort.
verses.1:8: For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning our affliction that occurred in Asia, that we were weighed down excessively, beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of living.
verses.1:9: Indeed, we ourselves had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we would not rely on ourselves, but on God who raises the dead;
verses.1:10: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue us; on Him we have set our hope that He will rescue us yet again,
verses.1:11: as you also join in helping on our behalf through prayer, so that for the gracious gift granted to us from many persons, thanks may be given through many on our behalf.
verses.1:12: For our boasting is this, the testimony of our conscience: that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we conducted ourselves in the world, and even more abundantly toward you.
verses.1:13: For we write nothing else to you except what you read or also understand; and I hope that you will understand until the end,
verses.1:14: just as you also have understood us in part, that we are your reason for boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
verses.1:15: And in this confidence I was intending to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace,
verses.1:16: and by way of you to pass through into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you to be sent on my way into Judea.
verses.1:17: Therefore, when I was intending this, did I really act with fickleness? Or the things that I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, so that with me there is "Yes, yes" and "No, no"?
verses.1:18: But God is faithful, that our word to you is not "Yes" and "No."
verses.1:19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you through us—through me and Silvanus and Timothy—was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it has become "Yes."
verses.1:20: For however many promises of God there are, in Him is the "Yes"; therefore also through Him is the "Amen" to God for glory through us.
verses.1:21: Now the One who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,
verses.1:22: who also sealed us and gave the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.1:23: But I call upon God as witness against my own soul, that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
verses.1:24: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers for your joy; for by faith you stand firm.
verses.2:1: For I decided this for myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.
verses.2:2: For if I cause you sorrow, then who is the one making me glad except the one who is made sorrowful by me?
verses.2:3: And I wrote this very thing so that when I came I would not have sorrow from those over whom I ought to rejoice, having confidence in all of you that my joy is that of you all.
verses.2:4: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you through many tears, not so that you might be made sorrowful, but so that you might know the love that I have more abundantly toward you.
verses.2:5: Now if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused sorrow to me, but in part—so as not to be too severe—to all of you.
verses.2:6: Sufficient for such a person is this punishment inflicted by the majority,
verses.2:7: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and comfort him, otherwise such a person might be swallowed up by excessive sorrow.
verses.2:8: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm love toward him.
verses.2:9: For to this end I also wrote, so that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
verses.2:10: Now whomever you forgive anything, I also do; for indeed what I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, I did it for your sake in the presence of Christ,
verses.2:11: so that we might not be taken advantage of by Satan; for we are not unaware of his designs.
verses.2:12: Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door had been opened for me in the Lord,
verses.2:13: I had no relief in my spirit because I did not find Titus my brother; instead, taking leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.
verses.2:14: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumphal procession in Christ and reveals through us the fragrance of the knowledge of Him in every place.
verses.2:15: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing;
verses.2:16: to the one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
verses.2:17: For we are not like the many, peddling the word of God; rather, as from sincerity, and as from God, in the sight of God we speak in Christ.
verses.3:1: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of commendation to you or from you?
verses.3:2: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed in our hearts, known and read by all people,
verses.3:3: being manifested that you are a letter of Christ, ministered by us, inscribed not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.
verses.3:4: And such confidence we have through Christ toward God.
verses.3:5: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to consider anything as coming from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God,
verses.3:6: who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, while the Spirit makes alive.
verses.3:7: Now if the ministry of death, engraved in letters on stones, came in glory, so that the sons of Israel could not gaze steadily at the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, which was being done away with,
verses.3:8: how will the ministry of the Spirit not be even more in glory?
verses.3:9: For if the ministry of condemnation had glory, much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory.
verses.3:10: For indeed, what was glorified has not been glorified in this respect, on account of the surpassing glory;
verses.3:11: for if what was being done away with came through glory, much more is what remains in glory.
verses.3:12: Having such a hope, therefore, we use great boldness,
verses.3:13: and are not like Moses, who used to put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel would not gaze steadily at the end of what was being done away with.
verses.3:14: But their minds were hardened. For until this very day the same veil remains unlifted at the reading of the old covenant, because in Christ it is done away with;
verses.3:15: but to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
verses.3:16: Yet whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
verses.3:17: And the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
verses.3:18: And we all, with unveiled face, seeing as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit.
verses.4:1: For this reason, having this ministry as we were shown mercy, we do not lose heart,
verses.4:2: but we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every human conscience before God.
verses.4:3: Yet even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing,
verses.4:4: among whom the god of this age blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that the illumination of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, would not shine forth.
verses.4:5: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your slaves for the sake of Jesus.
verses.4:6: For God, who said, "Out of darkness light will shine," is the One who shone in our hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
verses.4:7: Now we have this treasure in clay vessels, so that the extraordinary greatness of the power may be God's and not from us;
verses.4:8: afflicted in every way, yet not hemmed in; perplexed, yet not in despair;
verses.4:9: persecuted, yet not abandoned; thrown down, yet not destroyed;
verses.4:10: always carrying about in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our body.
verses.4:11: For we who live are constantly being handed over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh.
verses.4:12: So then, death is at work in us, but life in you.
verses.4:13: Now having the same spirit of faith, according to what has been written, "I believed; therefore I spoke," we also believe, and therefore we also speak,
verses.4:14: knowing that the One who raised Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and will present us with you.
verses.4:15: For all things are for your sake, so that grace, having increased through more people, may cause thanksgiving to overflow to the glory of God.
verses.4:16: Therefore we do not lose heart; but even though our outer person is decaying, still our inner person is being renewed day by day.
verses.4:17: For the momentary lightness of our affliction is producing for us far beyond all measure an eternal weight of glory,
verses.4:18: since we do not look at the things that are seen, but at the things that are unseen; for the things that are seen are temporary, whereas the things that are unseen are eternal.
verses.5:1: For we know that if our earthly house, the tent, is dismantled, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
verses.5:2: For indeed in this we groan, longing to be clothed over with our dwelling from heaven,
verses.5:3: if indeed, having been clothed, we will not be found naked.
verses.5:4: For indeed, we who are in the tent groan, being burdened, because we do not want to be unclothed, but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.5:5: Now the One who prepared us for this very purpose is God, who gave us the down payment of the Spirit.
verses.5:6: Therefore, being always confident and knowing that while we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord—
verses.5:7: for we walk by faith, not by appearance—
verses.5:8: yet we are confident, and we prefer rather to be away from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
verses.5:9: Therefore we also make it our aim, whether at home or away, to be well-pleasing to Him.
verses.5:10: For all of us must be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive back the deeds done through the body according to what he practiced, whether good or evil.
verses.5:11: Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade people, yet to God we have been made manifest; and I hope that we have been made manifest in your consciences as well.
verses.5:12: We are not commending ourselves to you again, but are giving you an occasion for boasting on our behalf, so that you may have an answer for those who boast in appearance and not in heart.
verses.5:13: For if we were out of our minds, it was for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
verses.5:14: For the love of Christ compels us, having concluded this, that One died on behalf of all; therefore all died;
verses.5:15: and He died on behalf of all, so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for the One who died and was raised on their behalf.
verses.5:16: Consequently, from now on we know no one according to the flesh; even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know Him that way.
verses.5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: the old things have passed away; look, new things have come into being!
verses.5:18: Now all these things are from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation,
verses.5:19: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
verses.5:20: Therefore we serve as ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were appealing through us; we implore you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
verses.5:21: He made the One who did not know sin to be sin on our behalf, so that we might become God's righteousness in Him.
verses.6:1: And working together, we also appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain;
verses.6:2: for He says, "At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you." Look, now is the acceptable time; look, now is the day of salvation—
verses.6:3: giving no cause for offense in anything, so that the ministry will not be found fault with,
verses.6:4: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in dire straits,
verses.6:5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in disturbances, in toils, in sleepless nights, in fastings,
verses.6:6: in purity, in knowledge, in forbearance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without hypocrisy,
verses.6:7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; through the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and the left,
verses.6:8: through honor and dishonor, through bad report and good report; as impostors, yet truthful;
verses.6:9: as unknown, yet well known; as dying, and look, we live; as disciplined, yet not put to death;
verses.6:10: as grieving, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
verses.6:11: Our mouth stands open to you, Corinthians; our heart has opened wide.
verses.6:12: You are not hemmed in by us, rather you are hemmed in within your own affections;
verses.6:13: now in equal return—I speak as to children—open wide yourselves also.
verses.6:14: Do not become unequally yoked with unbelievers; for what partnership do righteousness and lawlessness have, or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
verses.6:15: And what harmony does Christ have with Beliar, or what portion does a believer have with an unbeliever?
verses.6:16: And what agreement does the temple of God have with idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said, "I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people."
verses.6:17: "Therefore, come out from their midst and be separate," says the Lord, "and do not touch anything unclean; and I will welcome you,
verses.6:18: and I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to Me," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:1: Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.
verses.7:2: Make room for us; we wronged no one, we corrupted no one, we took advantage of no one.
verses.7:3: I do not say this for condemnation, for I have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and to live together.
verses.7:4: Great is my boldness toward you; great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort; I overflow with joy in all our affliction.
verses.7:5: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were afflicted in every way—conflicts outside, fears inside—
verses.7:6: yet God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
verses.7:7: and not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted over you, as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
verses.7:8: For even if I grieved you with the letter, I do not regret it; even if I did regret it (I see that that letter grieved you, even if for a while),
verses.7:9: now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved into repentance; for you were grieved according to God, so that in nothing you might suffer loss from us.
verses.7:10: For grief according to God produces repentance leading to salvation without regret, whereas the grief of the world produces death.
verses.7:11: For look at how much earnestness this very thing, being grieved according to God, produced in you—indeed what defense, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! In everything you proved yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
verses.7:12: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong, nor on account of the one who was wronged, but in order that your earnestness on our behalf might be revealed to you before God.
verses.7:13: Because of this we have been comforted. And in addition to our comfort, we rejoiced even more abundantly at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
verses.7:14: For if I have boasted to him at all on your behalf, I was not put to shame; but just as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting before Titus proved to be truth.
verses.7:15: And his affection is even more abundant toward you as he remembers the obedience of all of you, how you received him with fear and trembling.
verses.7:16: I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.
verses.8:1: Now we make known to you, brothers, the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia,
verses.8:2: that in a severe test of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded into the wealth of their generosity.
verses.8:3: For according to their ability, I testify, and beyond their ability, of their own accord,
verses.8:4: begging us with much urging for the grace and the sharing in the ministry to the saints—
verses.8:5: and not as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us through the will of God,
verses.8:6: so that we urged Titus that, just as he had previously begun, so he would also complete among you this grace as well.
verses.8:7: But just as you abound in everything—in faith and speech and knowledge and all earnestness and in the love from us in you—see that you abound in this grace also.
verses.8:8: I am not speaking by way of command, but proving through the earnestness of others the genuineness of your love as well.
verses.8:9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that on your account He became poor, even though He was rich, so that by His poverty you might become rich.
verses.8:10: And in this matter I give my opinion, for this is beneficial for you, who previously began from last year not only to do it, but also to desire it.
verses.8:11: But now complete the doing of it as well, so that just as there was the eagerness to desire it, so also there may be the completion of it out of what you have.
verses.8:12: For if the eagerness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
verses.8:13: For this is not so that there may be relief for others and affliction for you, but as a matter of equality:
verses.8:14: at the present time your abundance is for their need, so that their abundance may also be for your need, in order that there may be equality;
verses.8:15: just as it is written: "The one with much did not have too much, and the one with little did not have too little."
verses.8:16: Now thanks be to God, who puts the same earnestness on your behalf into the heart of Titus,
verses.8:17: because he indeed welcomed our appeal, yet being even more earnest, he has gone out to you of his own accord.
verses.8:18: And we have sent with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is throughout all the churches—
verses.8:19: and not only that, but he was also appointed by the churches as our travel companion in this grace that is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord Himself and our own eagerness—
verses.8:20: guarding against this, so that no one may find fault with us in this abundant gift that is being administered by us;
verses.8:21: for we aim at what is honorable not only before the Lord, but also before people.
verses.8:22: And we have sent with them our brother whom we have often tested in many things and found earnest, and now much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.
verses.8:23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you; as for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
verses.8:24: Therefore, display to them the proof of your love and of our boasting on your behalf, before the face of the churches.
verses.9:1: For concerning the ministry to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you,
verses.9:2: for I know your eagerness, about which I boast on your behalf to the Macedonians, that Achaia has been prepared since last year; and your zeal has stirred up the majority of them.
verses.9:3: Yet I have sent the brothers so that our boast on your behalf might not prove empty in this respect, in order that, just as I was saying, you may be prepared,
verses.9:4: otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to say you—would be put to shame in this confidence.
verses.9:5: Therefore I considered it necessary to urge the brothers to go ahead to you and arrange beforehand your previously promised blessing, so that it may be ready as a blessing and not as greed.
verses.9:6: Now consider this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows with blessings will also reap with blessings.
verses.9:7: Let each one give just as he has resolved in his heart, not out of grief or out of necessity, for God loves a joyful giver.
verses.9:8: And God is able to make every grace abound toward you, so that in everything, at all times, having all sufficiency, you may abound for every good work
verses.9:9: (just as it is written: "He scattered abroad, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever";
verses.9:10: and the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed and increase the yield of your righteousness),
verses.9:11: being enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces through us thanksgiving to God—
verses.9:12: for the ministry of this service is not only fully supplying the needs of the saints, but also abounding through many thanksgivings to God—
verses.9:13: through the proof of this ministry, they glorify God for the submission of your confession to the gospel of Christ and for the generosity of your sharing toward them and toward all,
verses.9:14: and in their prayer on your behalf, longing for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.
verses.9:15: Thanks be to God for His gift beyond description.
verses.10:1: Now I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the gentleness and forbearance of Christ—I who am humble face to face among you, yet bold toward you when absent;
verses.10:2: and I ask that when present I may not need to be bold with the confidence with which I count on acting daringly against certain ones who count us as walking according to the flesh.
verses.10:3: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh—
verses.10:4: for the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly, but powerful before God for tearing down strongholds—tearing down reasonings
verses.10:5: and every lofty thing raised up against the knowledge of God, and capturing every thought into the obedience of Christ,
verses.10:6: and standing ready to punish every disobedience, whenever your obedience has been fulfilled.
verses.10:7: You are looking at what is on the surface. If anyone is confident in himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this again within himself, that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.
verses.10:8: For even if I should boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame,
verses.10:9: so that I may not appear as though trying to frighten you through the letters;
verses.10:10: for "The letters," one says, "are weighty and forceful, yet the presence of the body is weak and the speech is despised."
verses.10:11: Let such a person consider this, that what we are in word through letters when absent, such we are also when present in deed.
verses.10:12: For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves; instead, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, they lack understanding.
verses.10:13: We, however, will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the sphere which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even as far as you—
verses.10:14: for we are not overextending ourselves as though we did not reach to you, since we arrived even as far as you in the gospel of Christ—
verses.10:15: not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, but having hope that as your faith increases, we will be enlarged among you according to our sphere to overflowing,
verses.10:16: to proclaim the gospel in the regions beyond you, not to boast in another's sphere over things already made ready.
verses.10:17: But let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord;
verses.10:18: for it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
verses.11:1: I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness; indeed, do bear with me!
verses.11:2: For I am jealous for you with God's jealousy; for I betrothed you to one husband, to present a pure virgin to Christ.
verses.11:3: Yet I fear that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by its craftiness, your minds might be corrupted away from the sincerity and the purity toward Christ.
verses.11:4: For if the one who comes proclaims another Jesus whom we did not proclaim, or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different gospel which you did not accept, you bear with it well enough.
verses.11:5: For I consider myself to have fallen short in nothing compared to the super-apostles;
verses.11:6: and even if I am unskilled in speech, yet not in knowledge; rather, in every way we have made it manifest to you in all things.
verses.11:7: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed the gospel of God to you free of charge?
verses.11:8: I plundered other churches, taking wages for the ministry to you,
verses.11:9: and when I was present with you and was in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my need; and in everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and I will keep doing so.
verses.11:10: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting will not be silenced in my case in the regions of Achaia.
verses.11:11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
verses.11:12: But what I am doing I will also continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those wanting an opportunity, in order that in the very thing in which they boast they may be found just as we are.
verses.11:13: For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
verses.11:14: And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
verses.11:15: Therefore it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness—whose end will be according to their works.
verses.11:16: Again I say, let no one think me to be foolish—or if not, then accept me even as a foolish person, so that I too may boast a little.
verses.11:17: What I am speaking, I am not speaking according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
verses.11:18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
verses.11:19: For you gladly bear with the foolish, being wise yourselves;
verses.11:20: for you bear with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes advantage of you, if someone exalts himself, if someone strikes you in the face.
verses.11:21: To our disgrace I say it, as though we have been weak! Yet in whatever anyone dares—I speak in foolishness—I dare as well.
verses.11:22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they offspring of Abraham? So am I.
verses.11:23: Are they servants of Christ? I speak as one out of his mind—I am even more so! In labors far more, in prisons far more, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths often;
verses.11:24: five times from the Jews I received forty lashes minus one,
verses.11:25: three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day I have spent in the deep;
verses.11:26: on journeys often, in dangers from rivers, in dangers from robbers, in dangers from my own people, in dangers from Gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the wilderness, in dangers at sea, in dangers among false brothers,
verses.11:27: in labor and hardship, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness;
verses.11:28: apart from the other things, there is the daily pressure on me: the anxiety for all the churches.
verses.11:29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led to stumble, and I do not burn?
verses.11:30: If it is necessary to boast, I will boast of the things concerning my weakness.
verses.11:31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, He who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
verses.11:32: In Damascus, the ethnarch under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
verses.11:33: and through a window I was lowered in a basket through the wall, and I escaped his hands.
verses.12:1: It is necessary to boast; it is not beneficial indeed, yet I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
verses.12:2: I know a man in Christ fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows—such a one was caught up as far as the third heaven.
verses.12:3: And I know such a man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know; God knows—
verses.12:4: that he was caught up into paradise and heard inexpressible words, which it is not permitted for a person to speak.
verses.12:5: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on behalf of myself I will not boast, except in weaknesses.
verses.12:6: For if I should wish to boast, I will not be foolish, for I will speak the truth; yet I refrain, so that no one may think of me beyond what he sees in me or hears from me,
verses.12:7: even because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations. Therefore, so that I would not become overly exalted, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan, to strike me repeatedly, so that I would not become overly exalted.
verses.12:8: Concerning this I pleaded with the Lord three times that it might depart from me;
verses.12:9: and He has said to me, "My grace is enough for you, for power is brought to completion in weakness." Most gladly, therefore, I will rather boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell upon me.
verses.12:10: Therefore I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions and distresses, on behalf of Christ; for whenever I am weak, then I am powerful.
verses.12:11: I have become foolish; you forced me to it! For I ought to have been commended by you. For I fell short in nothing compared to the super-apostles, even though I am nothing;
verses.12:12: indeed, the signs of an apostle were carried out among you with all endurance, by signs and wonders and works of power.
verses.12:13: For in what respect were you treated as inferior to the rest of the churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
verses.12:14: Look, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden; for I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children ought not to store up for their parents, but parents for their children.
verses.12:15: And I will most gladly spend and be completely spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved less?
verses.12:16: But let it be so: I myself did not weigh you down; yet, being crafty, I caught you by deceit.
verses.12:17: Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I have sent to you?
verses.12:18: I urged Titus and sent the brother along with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Not in the same footsteps?
verses.12:19: Have you been thinking all this time that we are defending ourselves to you? Before God in Christ we speak. And all things, beloved, are for your building up,
verses.12:20: for I fear that somehow when I come I may not find you such as I wish, and I may be found by you such as you do not wish—that somehow there may be strife, jealousy, outbursts of rage, selfish ambitions, slanders, whisperings, arrogant conceits, disorders;
verses.12:21: and that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many of those who have previously sinned and have not repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and sensuality that they practiced.
verses.13:1: This is the third time I am coming to you. By the mouth of two or three witnesses every matter will be established.
verses.13:2: I have warned beforehand and I still warn—as when present the second time, so now while absent—those who sinned earlier and all the rest, that if I come again I will not spare them,
verses.13:3: since you are seeking proof of Christ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you, but is powerful in you.
verses.13:4: For indeed He was crucified out of weakness, yet He lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him by the power of God toward you.
verses.13:5: Test yourselves as to whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not realize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you—unless indeed you are unapproved?
verses.13:6: But I hope that you will come to know that we are not unapproved.
verses.13:7: Now we pray to God that you do nothing wrong—not so that we may appear approved, but so that you may do what is right, even though we may be as though unapproved.
verses.13:8: For we are not able to do anything against the truth, but on behalf of the truth.
verses.13:9: For we rejoice whenever we are weak while you are strong. This also is what we pray for: your restoration.
verses.13:10: For this reason I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I may not act severely according to the authority that the Lord gave me, for building up and not for tearing down.
verses.13:11: Finally, brothers, rejoice, be restored, be encouraged, be of the same mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you.
verses.13:12: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
verses.13:13: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

notes.1:10: The critical text reads the future "will rescue" twice (ῥύσεται ... ῥύσεται); other manuscripts read the present "rescues" (ῥύεται) or omit the first clause.
notes.1:11: The Greek phrases "from many persons" (lit. "faces") and "through many" can be construed either as prayer offered by many leading to the gift or as thanksgiving rising from many for the gift.
notes.1:12: The critical text reads "holiness" (ἁγιότητι); many later manuscripts read "simplicity" or "sincerity" (ἁπλότητι).
notes.1:22: "Down payment" (ἀρραβών) denotes a first installment that guarantees full payment to follow.
notes.2:5: Paul inserts the parenthetical phrase "in part—so as not to be too severe" to soften his statement that the offender caused sorrow to the entire congregation rather than to Paul alone.
notes.2:14: The verb θριαμβεύω ("lead in triumphal procession") evokes a Roman victory parade, though scholars debate whether Paul pictures apostles as conquered captives displayed by God or as participants in Christ's victory.
notes.2:17: "Peddling" (καπηλεύω) refers to huckstering or adulterating wares (such as wine) for personal profit.
notes.3:2: The critical text reads "in our hearts" (ἡμῶν); a few manuscripts read "in your hearts" (ὑμῶν).
notes.3:7: The verb καταργέω (also in vv. 11, 13, 14) means "render inoperative," "bring to an end," or "do away with."
notes.3:14: The conjunction ὅτι may be taken causally ("because in Christ it is done away with") or as content ("it not being unveiled that in Christ it is done away with").
notes.3:18: The middle participle κατοπτριζόμενοι is debated between "seeing as in a mirror" and "reflecting as a mirror"; the closing phrase ἀπὸ κυρίου πνεύματος may be rendered "from the Lord, the Spirit," "from the Spirit of the Lord," or "from the Lord who is the Spirit."
notes.4:4: The Greek infinitive "shine forth" (augasai) can be taken intransitively with "the illumination" as its subject (as translated) or transitively ("so that they might not see the illumination").
notes.4:14: Some manuscripts read "the Lord Jesus" instead of "Jesus," and "through Jesus" instead of "with Jesus."
notes.4:15: The phrase "through more people" (dia ton pleionon) can modify either "having increased" or "may cause thanksgiving to overflow," and forms a wordplay with "increased" (pleonasasa).
notes.5:3: Some manuscripts read "having been unclothed" (ekdysamenoi) rather than "having been clothed" (endysamenoi); the conjunction "if indeed" (ei ge) can also carry a confident sense ("since indeed").
notes.5:7: Greek "eidos" denotes visible appearance or outward form, here contrasted with faith.
notes.5:17: The verbless Greek clause "kaine ktisis" may be understood either cosmically ("there is a new creation") or individually ("that person is a new creature"); later manuscripts add "all things" (ta panta) to the final clause.
notes.5:21: Greek "hamartia" ("sin") here may carry the sense of "sin offering" (as often in the Septuagint).
notes.6:1: The participle "working together" (synergountes) lacks an explicit object in Greek, leaving open whether Paul means working together with God (cf. 1 Cor 3:9) or alongside his fellow ministers.
notes.6:12: Greek "splagchna" literally denotes the inward parts as the seat of deep emotion and is translated "affections."
notes.6:15: Beliar is a Greek spelling of Belial (meaning "worthlessness" or "wickedness"), used in Jewish writings of the Second Temple period as a name for Satan.
notes.7:9: The phrase "according to God" (also in 7:10-11) literally denotes grief aligned with God's will and purpose, contrasted with "the grief of the world" in 7:10.
notes.7:10: The Greek adjective ametameleton ("without regret") can modify either "repentance" or "salvation"; the translated word order preserves that link.
notes.7:12: Some manuscripts reverse the pronouns to read "our earnestness on your behalf," though the critical text followed here reads "your earnestness on our behalf."
notes.8:2: Greek haplotēs literally means "singleness" or "sincerity" and in the context of the collection (also 9:11, 13) denotes wholehearted generosity.
notes.8:4: Verses 3-4 contain an ellipsis in Greek with no finite verb for giving; Paul breaks off the sentence and resumes in 8:5 with "they gave themselves."
notes.8:7: Some manuscripts read "your love for us," whereas the critical text followed here reads "the love from us in you."
notes.8:20: The noun hadrotēs ("abundant gift") occurs only here in the New Testament and refers to the large monetary collection administered by Paul and his coworkers.
notes.8:23: "Messengers" translates apostoloi, used here of commissioned delegates sent by the churches rather than the Twelve.
notes.9:4: The noun hypostasis ("confidence") denotes Paul's confident assurance or undertaking in boasting about the Corinthians; some later manuscripts add "of boasting."
notes.9:5: Paul plays on eulogia ("blessing," referring to a generous gift, continued in 9:6) contrasted with pleonexia ("greed," i.e., a sum extracted grudgingly).
notes.9:9: Quoting Psalm 112:9 (LXX 111:9), where the subject ("he") is the righteous, generous person who fears the Lord.
notes.9:15: The adjective anekdiēgētos ("beyond description") appears only here in the New Testament, meaning impossible to recount in full.
notes.10:4: Greek dynata to theo ("powerful before God") uses a dative that can mean "powerful in God's sight," "powerful for God," or (as an intensive idiom) "divinely powerful."
notes.10:7: The verb blepete can be construed either as an indicative ("You are looking at what is on the surface") or as an imperative ("Look at what is right before your face").
notes.10:13: Greek kanon ("sphere") refers to a measuring rod or boundary line defining the ministerial territory apportioned by God.
notes.11:1: The second anechesthe can be read either as an imperative ("indeed, do bear with me") or as an indicative ("indeed, you are bearing with me").
notes.11:3: Some manuscripts omit "and the purity" (kai tes hagnotetos), though it is strongly attested in early witnesses and echoes the "pure virgin" imagery of 11:2.
notes.11:6: The Greek participle phanerosantes is grammatically elliptical without a finite verb or explicit object; some manuscripts read the passive phanerothentes ("having been made manifest").
notes.11:28: Greek ton parektos can mean "the other things left unmentioned" or "the external troubles," and epistasis conveys a daily "pressure" or crowding of concerns.
notes.12:7: The opening phrase ("even because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations") may conclude v. 6 or begin v. 7; Greek skolops denotes a sharp "thorn," "splinter," or "stake."
notes.12:9: The earliest manuscripts read "power" (he dynamis) without "My" (later witnesses add mou); episkenose literally means "pitch its tent over" or "tabernacle upon."
notes.12:16: Paul appears to echo an ironic accusation from his critics that although he took no direct support, he craftily exploited the Corinthians through deceit.
notes.12:21: The adverb palin ("again") may modify elthontos mou ("when I come again") or the verb tapeinose ("humble me again").
notes.13:1: Echoes Deuteronomy 19:15; "by the mouth of" is an idiom for oral testimony, and the Greek noun rhema can mean either "word" or "matter/charge."
notes.13:5: Greek adokimoi ("unapproved") draws from testing or assaying imagery and means "failing the test" or "disqualified," carrying through verses 6-7 alongside dokimoi ("approved").
notes.13:11: Greek chairete can mean "rejoice" (echoing "we rejoice" in verse 9) or serve as a conventional closing greeting ("farewell").
notes.13:13: Following standard Greek versification, both greetings appear in 13:12 and the benediction is 13:13 (numbered 13:14 in many English versions); the earliest manuscripts do not include a closing "Amen."
